A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and two experiments. The main text, equations, figures, eight result tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated attribution results and renumbered prompts.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original WMT24++ translation experiments with GPT-4o-mini and Gemini-2.0-Flash, plus GPT-4o attribution judgments. Tables 1–8 and appendix analyses provide detailed outcomes.

after.justification: V2 retains the original translation comparisons, attribution judgments, per-language scores, and translation trajectories in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The Translate again procedure and translation and judging prompts are unchanged after matching v1 Appendix C to v2 Appendix B. V2 clarifies conversation-history handling without establishing a change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight English-to-target WMT24++ directions at segment and aggregated-input levels. Renaming the latter from document-level to paragraph-level clarifies the existing coverage; it does not introduce different data or a new scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Briakou et al.'s Step-by-step prompting and direct/zero-shot translation in the corresponding comparisons. Newly cited refinement and reasoning papers are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain 960 source samples, 221 aggregated inputs limited to 150 space-separated tokens, the same translation models, four prompting steps, four neural metrics, and COMET grouping thresholds. V2's context-handling disclosure and paragraph-metric rationale do not establish revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: The refinement analyses, language comparisons, trajectories in Figures 6–7, attribution analysis, and illustrated judge output are retained. V1's full attribution plot moves into v2's main text; early exit and multi-paragraph consistency are discussed without new tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates. The reporting practice of language averages, individual scores, and attribution counts remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain identical numerical results. However, v2 Section 4 adds the qualitative claim that the best results follow a single refinement, whereas v1 allows marginal gains thereafter. This new summary is too broad: retained Table 5 gives GPT-4o-mini Translate again mean COMET scores of 83.76 after one refinement and 84.19 after three.

T1.justification: The conditional-generation equations and faithfulness classification rules are unchanged. Section 5 replaces numerical superscripts with SS/TA labels and explicitly represents paired differences, clarifying the existing attribution procedure without adding mathematical results or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions argue that self-refinement accounts for most gains, decomposition offers unreliable benefits, and faithfulness need not improve translation. The human-versus-LLM strategy divergence emphasized in v2's abstract already appears in v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands interpretation: it contrasts compositional reasoning with holistic translation, questions same-model lexical preselection, identifies possible cross-paragraph consistency benefits outside the tested scope, and distinguishes components of reasoning. V2 also adds early-exit and judge-bias arguments while retaining the existing model-family and judge-diversity limitations.

D1.justification: V1 promises an anonymous release of 223k translations from three models; v2 announces and links code and 223k translations from two models. V2 also explicitly discloses retaining all prior context during proofreading, distinguishing its implementation from the cited original. The PDFs do not establish a rerun.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chen et al. (2024a) on iterative translation refinement, Deutsch et al. (2023) on paragraph evaluation, and Guo et al. (2025) and Muennighoff et al. (2025) on reasoning models. These support limited contextual extensions; other publication-year and venue updates retain the same cited works.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted abstract, conclusion, and attribution-explanation edits, standardizes paragraph-level terminology, and adds Discussion and Acknowledgements sections. The central narrative remains intact, with the redundant attribution appendix removed and prompt appendices renumbered.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the abbreviated main-text attribution plot with the full eight-language plot previously in v1 Figure 8, using a common vertical scale across groups. Captions, paragraph labels, and figure numbering change, while other figures and table structures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through more accurate paragraph-level scope, explicit context-handling disclosure, and concrete code/data access information. The expanded discussion and consolidated attribution figure improve interpretation of the retained evidence. These gains are tempered by the new blanket one-refinement optimum claim, which is not consistently supported by the unchanged tables.
